medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
The office of admissions sponsors the PROMISE (Promoting Recruitment Opportunities in Medicine with Individual Study Experiences) program. This program is for those who are socially or economically disadvantaged or those who are from rural or medically underserved areas. PROMISE is geared toward those who are sophomores in college.  The Mississippi Rural Physicians Scholarship Program (MRPSP) is geared toward those from rural areas. The Professional Portal Program (PPP) is geared toward those who are socially or economically disadvantaged or those from rural or medically underserved areas. The PPP is geared toward those students who are upper level or have graduated from college.
Additionally, there are several outreach programs held that target students from groups traditionally underrepresented in medicine, from rural or medically underserved areas, or those who are economically or educationally disadvantaged.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Leave of absence from medical school may be granted by the Dean or his administrative designee under the following conditions: 1. For students in good academic standing to pursue training as a medical scientist (i.e., to pursue research experience or to complete a Masters or Ph.D. degree). 2. For students with academic, personal, financial or medical problems in special circumstances. If the leave of absence is granted during the academic year for the remainder of that academic year with the potential of returning to repeat the entire academic year, final grades in courses which have been completed will be recorded in the Office of the Registrar. Grades in courses in progress shall be reported to the Office of the Registrar as "withdrawn".
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
The Associated Student Body is the student government association for the University Medical Center schools of medicine, dentistry, nursing, health related professions, pharmacy, and graduate studies in the health sciences. It provides a mechanism to voice student concerns, ideas, and questions to the administration and community. For more information see, https://www.umc.edu/Office%20of%20Academic%20Affairs/For-Students/Student%20Affairs/Associated-Student-Body/Overview.html
 The Norman C. Nelson Student Union houses the campus bookstore, a food court, ASB offices as well as meeting and event space.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The Medical Center is located on a 164-acre campus in Jackson. The state capital and Mississippi's largest city, Jackson offers a wide array of professional arts attractions. Recreational facilities include a 30,000-acre reservoir located 15 minutes from the campus.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Rent averages from $1200 -!400 per month for area apartments.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Tutoring is available for eligible students free of charge for the first 20 hours each semester.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: These are completed within the University hospitals and clinics, the Jackson VA and statewide preceptor sites.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Required attendance of 80% of in-person instruction.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: During the two preclinical years, students learn the sciences basic to the study of medicine and participate in laboratory exercises, small-group discussion, computer-assisted learning, and independent study. The preclinical curriculum integrates and sequences course content and provides earlier clinical experience for students. The third year involves full-time clinical study as students rotate through the major clinical disciplines and participate in the team care of patients in the University Hospitals and Clinics, Veterans Affairs Medical Center, and various community settings. The fourth year consists of eight required calendar month blocks that may be taken at any time during the eleven months available from July through May. Fourth-year clinical clerkships provide greater depth of study in core areas of medicine, as well as in a student's anticipated medical specialty. Opportunities exist for advanced study and research in basic science departments and for electives at other ins
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
In 2007 the Mississippi Legislature created the Mississippi Rural Physicians Scholarship Program (MRPSP) 
https://www.umc.edu/Office%20of%20Academic%20Affairs/For-Students/Academic%20Outreach%20Programs/Mississippi%20Rural%20Physicians%20Scholarship%20Program/Mississippi%20Rural%20Physicians%20Scholarship%20Program.html
Which created a unique longitudinal program that identifies rural college students who aspire to return to their roots to practice medicine. The MRPSP mission is to nurture future rural physicians in three phases from college through residency training. 
The SOM also is the recipient of a HRSA grant entitle Impact The Race which supports training in rural areas in Mississippi.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
The Office of Research promotes excellence in scholarship and research at UMMC and facilitates translation of research discoveries to improve human health. More information can be found here.  https://www.umc.edu/Research/Research_Home.html
Some major research initiatives include Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study (ARIC) and the Jackson Heart Study https://www.jacksonheartstudy.org/ ) sponsored by the National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute.  Many other research opportunities are available through the various school of medicine departments at UMMC.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students are required to spend time at the student run Jackson Free Clinic
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Optional, except for MD/PHD students or the longitudinal Medical Student Research Program (MSRP).
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: The University of Mississippi Medical Center is proud to have clinical site affiliations with a number of hospitals throughout Mississippi.  In addition, UMMC owns or leases community hospitals.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The School of Medicine, created by a special act of the Board of Trustees in June 1903, operated as a two-year school in Oxford until 1955, when it expanded to four years and moved to the new University of Mississippi Medical Center in Jackson. The Medical Center now houses the Schools of Medicine, Nursing, Health Related Professions, Dentistry, Graduate Studies in Health Sciences, Population Health, and the 722-bed University Hospitals and Health System.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The University of Mississippi School of Medicine is committed to training skilled and compassionate physicians to provide high-quality and equitable health care particularly to the state’s residents, including diverse and underserved populations.  The school prepares learners to provide excellent care through programs of innovative education, state-of-the-art research and comprehensive clinical practice.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks; but multiple acceptances may be held until April 30th
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
At least 2 letters must be from instructors who have taught the student a course. 1 letter can be from a research advisor or premed advisor.
Shadowing or employment letters do not fulfill the 3 letter requirement. They may be submitted as supplementary letters, but no more than 5 total letters will be accepted.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Students arrive by 7:30 A.M. on interview day. Interviews conclude by 1:00 P.M. and include lunch and a tour with current medical students.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: URL to Applicant Portal provided after receipt of verified AMCAS application.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Must be either a permanent resident or US citizen with Mississippi residency to apply (please read residency rules). Must have course requirements from an accredited U.S College or University.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The SOM employs a balanced admissions review that affords each applicant balanced consideration of life experiences, personal attributes, and academic metrics to select not only those who can succeed but those who should be admitted based on the school mission.  For further details, see Applicant Evaluation and Decisions on the School of Medicine Admissions website.

The School of Medicine offers pre-application counseling for prospective applicants and post-application counseling for unsuccessful applicants. To make an appointment, call the admissions office at 601-984-5010.  The Admissions Office encourages all students who are interested in applying to our SOM to arrange for pre-counseling early in their undergraduate career.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: We consider MCAT scores as one part of the entire application.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Strong preference is given to applicants who will have completed all requirements for a baccalaureate degree prior to entering medical school. For those applicants applying with the minimum 90 acceptable semester hours, a maximum of 65 semester hours of credit from an accredited community college may be applied toward the minimum 90 acceptable semester hours required for admission. College graduates may complete additional post-baccalaureate coursework to satisfy prerequisites at any accredited U.S. college or university, regardless of the number of community college credit hours applied toward their completed undergraduate degree.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
Students must demonstrate the acquisition of essential skills and professional attitudes and behaviors. To meet these expectations, all students must have the necessary abilities to navigate a rigorous curriculum, participate in patient care activities in varying clinical settings, and provide patient care safely and effectively.  (1) Observation, (2) Communication, (3) Motor and Sensory Function, (4) Intellectual, Cognitive, and Conceptual Skills, and (5) Behavioral, Social, and Professional attributes.
The School of Medicine complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act and other applicable laws, striving to provide reasonable accommodations to qualified students with disabilities. However, all students must be able to independently perform the essential functions of the curriculum without the assistance of intermediaries that would alter their judgment or the nature of the required tasks. Meeting these standards must be possible with or without reasonable accommodations.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
Accepted students may apply for financial aid. The school participates in federal scholarship and loan programs (such as Perkins and Stafford) and state-funded Mississippi Rural Physician Scholarship and State Medical Education Loan/Scholarship programs. Eligible students may qualify for limited scholarship funds provided by private donors. For additional financial aid details, see 
https://www.umc.edu/som/Departments%20and%20Offices/SOM%20Administrative%20Offices/SOM%20Admissions/Overview.html
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: It is the intent of the University of Mississippi Medical Center to provide the highest quality education at a reasonable cost. Since student tuition and fee charges are used for operating costs, including scholarships and waivers, the Medical Center reserves the right to increase or modify tuition and fees without prior notice subject to the approval of the Board of Trustees of State Institutions of Higher Learning.
